scope: Server-produced immutable drop/pickup descriptors bind actor, loot generation, exact metadata, transferred/remainder quantities, instance, position, loot ownership/party and original timing.

Full character effects reuse existing private ItemDeliveryReceipts; no new private character format is introduced. Receipt replay precedes capacity and item-presence checks and cannot recreate consumed gear or repeat collection progress.

Pure drop preparation does not debit/publish. Pickup preparation reserves its exact recipient/fingerprint before IO; reservations reject ordinary pickup and survive expiry, including a deferred-removal recheck.

Projection changes require a matching supplied saved-character receipt. Process-local bounded publication guards prevent source replay refilling a partial stack or republishing collected loot; these guards are explicitly not durable custody after restart.

Exact-metadata stack planning separates different same-name affixes/qualities. Newly split bag stacks have stable separate IDs; duplicated source IDs across bag/equipment/stash/buyback fail preparation. Legacy implicit single units and empty omitted metadata remain transferable.
Ground-item entity snapshots now deep-copy mutable gear metadata. Private reservation/origin/generation/hash fields stay outside public JSON.
